chunks: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.

The blessed Shaykh, the Imam, the felicitous jurist, [resident of al-Rayy], Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, the compiler of this book—may Allah sanctify his soul—said: To proceed: when the divine decree drove me to the lands of estrangement, and destiny brought me from there to the land of Balkh, in the district of Ilaq, there came to it al-Sharif al-Din Abu 'Abd Allah, known as Ni'mah—and he is Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ishaq ibn [al-Hasan ibn] al-Husayn ibn Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them. My joy endured through his company, my breast expanded through his recollection, and my honor was greatly ennobled through his affection, because of qualities he had gathered together along with his nobility: concealment, righteousness, tranquility, dignity, religiosity, chastity, taqwa, and humility.

Then he mentioned to me a book compiled by Muhammad ibn Zakariyya, the physician al-Razi, which he entitled the book Man La Yahduruhu al-Tabib, and he said that it was sufficient in its purpose. He asked me to compile for him a book in fiqh, halal and haram, statutes and rulings, encompassing all that I had authored on that subject, and that I entitle it Kitab Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih, so that it might be his point of reference, his basis of reliance, and the source from which he would take, and that whoever looks into it, copies it, and acts upon what is deposited in it might share in its reward. This was along with his having copied most of my compilations that accompanied me, having heard them, narrated them from me, and become acquainted with their totality, and they were two hundred and forty-five books.

So I answered him—may Allah perpetuate his tawfiq—in that, because I found him worthy of it. I compiled this book for him by omitting the asanid so that its routes would not become too numerous, even if its benefits are many. I did not intend in it the aim of the compilers in citing everything they narrated; rather, I intended to cite what I give fatwa upon, judge to be sound, and hold to be a hujjah between me and my Lord—sanctified is His remembrance and exalted is His power.

All that is in it has been extracted from famous books upon which reliance is placed and to which recourse is made, such as the book of Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sijistani, the book of 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, the books of 'Ali ibn Mahziyar al-Ahwazi, the books of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, the Nawadir of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, the book Nawadir al-Hikmah compiled by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, the book al-Rahmah by Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, the Jami' of our Shaykh Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, the books of al-Mahasin by Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Barqi, and the epistle of my father—may Allah be pleased with him—besides other usul and compilations whose paths of transmission to me are known in the catalogue of the books that I narrated from my mashayikh and forefathers—may Allah be pleased with them.

I exerted my utmost effort in that, seeking help from Allah, relying upon Him, and seeking forgiveness for deficiency. And my tawfiq is only by Allah; upon Him I have relied and to Him I turn, and He is sufficient for me, and the best trustee.

ai.seo_question: Why did Shaykh al-Saduq compile Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih and what sources did he rely on?
ai.summary: This prelude explains why Shaykh al-Saduq compiled Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih and the method he followed in it. He states that he omitted the sanad/isnad, included only what he gives fatwa upon and deems authoritative, and derived the work from well-known foundational Shia books.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: In the name of Allah (swt), the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The honourable Shaykh Al Jaleel, and jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, the author of this book-may Allah (swt) sanctify his soul-wrote:
After praise to Allah (swt), it happened that fate drove me to the lands of exile, and destiny brought me to the land of Balkh, specifically the town of Ilaq. There arrived the noble Sharif al-Din Abu Abdullah, known as Ni'mah-Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ishaq ibn [al-Hasan ibn] al-Husayn ibn Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all).
With his companionship, my happiness was prolonged, my heart was comforted by his memory, and my honor was elevated by his affection, due to his noble character combined with virtues such as modesty, piety, calmness, dignity, religiosity, chastity, godliness, and humility.

He mentioned to me a book authored by Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi, the physician, titled Man La Yahduruhu al-Tabeeb (For Him Who Has No Access to a Doctor), which he found to be effective in its purpose. He requested that I compile for him a book on jurisprudence, covering lawful and unlawful matters, and the statutes and rulings, comprehensively surpassing all I had previously written on the subject, and title it Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih (For Him Who Has No Access to a Jurist). The intention was for it to serve as his reference, foundation, and guide-one through which he could achieve reward, along with those who read, copy, or act upon its contents.
This was in addition to his copying most of what I carried with me from my works, listening to them, narrating them from me, and familiarizing himself with their entirety, which amounted to two hundred and forty-five books.

I agreed to his request (may Allah (swt) grant him continuous success) because I found him deserving of it. I compiled this book by omitting the chains of narration to avoid excessive length, while ensuring its benefits were plentiful. I did not intend to follow the approach of other compilers who include all they have narrated. Instead, I included only what I issue fatwas upon, deem to be authentic, and believe to be a proof between me and my Lord (azj) -exalted be His remembrance and elevated be His power.

Everything in this book is derived from well-known books that are relied upon and referenced, such as the book of Hariz ibn Abdullah al-Sijistani, the book of Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, the works of Ali ibn Mahziyar al-Ahwazi, the books of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, the Nawadir of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, the Nawadir al-Hikmah compiled by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, the Kitab al-Rahmah by Sa'd ibn Abdullah, the compilation of our Sheikh Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may Allah (swt) be pleased with them), the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, the books of al-Muhasin by Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, the letters of my father (may Allah be pleased with them), and other foundational texts and compilations.
The paths to these works are well-known in the catalog of books I have narrated from my teachers and predecessors (may Allah (swt) be pleased with them).

I have exerted my utmost effort in this task, seeking Allah's (swt) assistance, placing my trust in Him, and asking forgiveness for any shortcomings. My success is only through Allah (swt). Upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn. He is sufficient for me, and He is the best trustee.
